# Start Here

An Alkahest book is intentionally small. You write Markdown, keep a few facts in
`book.toml`, and use ordinary `make` commands. The engine generates Quarto and
backend-specific configuration in disposable build space.

## Check the prerequisites

You need Make and rootless Podman. The container supplies Python, Quarto, the
PDF backends, fonts, and the Alkahest engine, so none of them must be installed
on the host.

Because this guide lives in the private engine repository, first run `make
bootstrap` at the repository root to build the engine image. Then run `make
bootstrap` here once to create the tiny book-facing image. A public book made
from the eventual GitHub template will pull a released engine image instead.

Run `make doctor` next. It validates the book configuration, counts the
chapters, and confirms the renderer inside the container. Routine author
commands run without network access and write host-owned output through the
mounted book directory.

## Know the files

| Path | What you own |
|---|---|
| `book.toml` | Title, author, language, excerpt selection, and optional theme changes |
| `manuscript/index.qmd` | Preface or introduction |
| `manuscript/chapters/` | Numbered chapters in reading order |
| `manuscript/appendices/` | Optional numbered appendices |
| `manuscript/references.qmd` | The generated bibliography location |
| `references.bib` | Citation records |
| `assets/` | Images and other public source assets |

Commit those files, the writer `Makefile`, and the small managed
`.alkahest/scaffold.json` identity record. Commit the book's `Containerfile`,
which pins its engine runtime, but do not copy engine code into the book or
commit `_build/`; the `.gitignore` already excludes build output.

## Build the first draft

Run:

```sh
make draft
```

This builds only the full HTML book, making it the quickest visual writing
loop. Open `_build/full/html/index.html` in a browser. A successful build prints
only the format being rendered and the output location; renderer diagnostics
remain visible when something fails.

Use `make help` whenever you forget a command. The book Makefile is the
complete routine interface, not a small sample of a larger command list.

::: {.callout-important}
Edit the authored files at the repository root. Never fix a problem by editing
`_build/.work/`; that directory is recreated by every check and build.
:::
